summary: The note announces the city's first Book Drive and Literacy Day, to be held September 10, 2023 at the local community center, organized to promote literacy and its link to economic progress. The event combines a book collection of over 10,000 books with interactive activities, digital literacy workshops, and expert panels. Organizers also plan a long-term, year-round campaign supported by more than 200 volunteers.
one_line: The city's first Book Drive and Literacy Day on September 10, 2023 aims to collect over 10,000 books and promote literacy and economic growth.
key_facts: The inaugural Book Drive and Literacy Day will be held on September 10, 2023 at the local community center, with doors opening at 9 a.m.
The event is a collaboration between the City Library, several local bookstores, the Community Outreach Program, and the Our City Reads Foundation.
Jennifer Hart, president of the Our City Reads Foundation, said "Literacy is not just about reading; it's about empowerment and progress."
A study by the National Literary Trust found that regions with higher literacy rates often see enhanced economic conditions.
Local economist Jason Kemper said "Investing in literacy is investing in our economy."
The Book Drive expects to collect over 10,000 donated books from residents, libraries, and local businesses.
Ryan Carver, the City Library Director, said the drive also focuses on accessibility, relevance, and diversity in reading material for different age groups and interests.
A significant portion of the collected books will create minilibraries in underprivileged areas and restock school libraries that have faced budget cuts.
Educational counselors will be on-site to guide attendees on selecting reading materials and enhancing reading skills.

Literacy Day activities include read-aloud sessions, storytelling corners, workshops by local authors, literacy games, writing workshops, and panel discussions; Maria Gonzalez, an elementary school reading specialist, is involved in planning.
Partnering with local tech firms, organizers will offer workshops on e-readers and online libraries and supply e-readers preloaded with books to those without easy access to physical books.
Tom Rawlings, head of volunteer coordination, is overseeing more than 200 volunteers who will sort books, guide attendees, and manage the event.
Organizers plan an ongoing campaign after September 10 through book clubs, reading programs, and continuous community outreach.
